verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “I've had a sort of fairly sort of bad, severe headache for the past four days,” matching a severe headache for 4 days.
Patient states the sequence as, “So headache started first and then... fever sort of came along a bit afterwards,” so the headache was followed by fever, not preceded by it.

Patient reports feeling hot and thinks they have a fever but has not measured it: “I've been sort of feeling a bit hot as well... I haven't measured it, but I think I've got fever.” Doctor later summarizes hot and cold feelings.
Patient reports, “So I've had some paracetamol and some ibuprofen, but it's not really helping at the moment,” indicating both medications without relief.

On neck movement: patient says, “I've got sort of general aching muscles. Not necessary, sort of in my neck. It's kind of a bit all over, really,” supporting general myalgia and no specific neck pain or stiffness.
When asked about light sensitivity, patient says, “No, it's fine. Light doesn't seem to bother me too much,” which is denial of photophobia.

Doctor asks, “have you been sick with this headache?” and patient replies, “No, I haven't been sick,” supporting denial of vomiting/being sick; nausea is not mentioned but denial of being sick reasonably covers vomiting.
Doctor: “And do you have a cough?” Patient: “No, no cough.”
Doctor: “you, your ears are okay? There's no earaches?” Patient: “No, it seems to be. Okay, that's fine,” denying earache.

Doctor asks about pins and needles and weakness; patient replies, “No, no pins and needles,” and clarifies strength: “Seem to be fine with that sort of stuff,” supporting no neurological symptoms of paresthesia or weakness.

Patient describes rash: “It's rashes kind of all over my body… Sort of red and itchy.” Doctor asks about glass test: “if you put a glass on top of the rash, does that rash go away? Yes, it goes away,” confirming a diffuse red, itchy, blanching rash.
Patient: “I have been away to Thailand a week or so ago. I've had some like usual mosquito bites from sort of traveling around,” matching recent Thailand travel about a week ago with mosquito bites.
Patient adds, “and a friend of mine has also been a bit unwell,” confirming an unwell contact.
Doctor asks about shivering; patient replies, “I do feel cold quite a lot. You know, it's no sort of shivering, but definitely like a bit cold,” supporting no shivering but intermittent feeling cold.
When asked about medical conditions, patient replies, “No, general medical history is fine,” indicating no past medical history.
Doctor summarizes: “no surgical history that. No medical or surgical complaints? Yeah.” Patient agrees, “No,” supporting no past surgical history.
Doctor asks about regular medication: “are you on any regular, any medication…?” Patient answers, “No,” confirming no regular medications.
Patient: “So I've had some paracetamol… but it's not really helping at the moment,” indicating paracetamol without relief.
Same sentence: “So I've had some paracetamol and some ibuprofen, but it's not really helping at the moment,” confirming ibuprofen use without relief.
Doctor: “Any allergies at all?” Patient: “No,” confirming no allergies.

Doctor states limitation: “it is quite important for us to actually examine you… it's not possible for us to do that online,” and no physical findings are documented, so absence of objective exam is supported.

Doctor: “things that's running in the back of my mind are kind of viral illnesses that one can get with sort of mosquito bites or foreign travel… The other common thing around Thailand… will be like some dengue,” and notes blanching rash vs. dengue bleeding, matching suspicion of viral illness such as dengue/arbovirus after tropical travel.
Doctor explicitly mentions ruling out meningitis: “things like we have to rule out is meningitis and all,” indicating plan to exclude serious infections.

Doctor notes, “you just have a general muscle ache. You didn't say that you had things like you had problems looking at light or something,” and no focal neuro deficits are reported, supporting generalized myalgia without focal neurological signs.

Doctor: “I think you would need to come into one of our hubs to have a proper examination, and I think you would need one quite urgently… be seen… preferably in the next few hours time,” confirming urgent in-person exam today within hours.

Doctor states, “I would rather you see a GP as soon as possible… I think you need to be seen and maybe have some blood tests and examinations,” indicating plan to consider blood work and further diagnostics.
Doctor: “if that's not available, I'd like you to take yourself to A E,” advising attendance at A&E if urgent appointment unavailable.

While doctor discusses meningitis signs generally (problems with light, non-blanching rash), there is no explicit advice to the patient to monitor for worsening symptoms such as neck stiffness, photophobia, non-blanching rash, or neurological deficits, so this detailed monitoring instruction is not stated.
